column1: > A row whose source has no published commit yet is still built by a --src build
> and still left out of a --bin one. sources.tsv says which sources those are.
> A row the --bin route cannot fill must be gated in abstraction.wxs, because a
> gate is what turns a missing file into a smaller package instead of a red
> build. jobd.exe and jobdw.exe are separate console/windowless links of the
> same supervisor source and both have required rows below.
> over_curl.hpp has a declared abstraction-download-over-curl repository rule,
> but no public refs were present at the 2026-09-12 check. Until a public commit
> is verified, its optional source stays UNRESOLVED.
> The Panel ships no side-by-side manifest. Its two elements were a dpiAware
> setting that monitor/win/win_windows.go already applies by calling
> SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext, and a Common-Controls 6.0.0.0 dependency that
> names processorArchitecture="amd64" while this package is also built for arm64.
> It was also a copy row against the same source as the program, so a --bin
> release build could never obtain it, and its absence turned the whole Panel
> feature off and took the program with it. monitor/README.md documents the
> manual copy for anyone who wants the button styling in a local build.
> The four Python rows are gated on Dev for a different reason: they have a
> publishable source and no way to reach it from a package assembled out of
> published module versions, which is what the release builds. Those two
> packages publish on their own registry, and a redistributable carrying a
> second copy of them would be one file with two homes — the same answer
> posix/payload.tsv gives. A build handed --src job and --src download carries
> them; the release is not, and says so.
